verdict_text:
YES

The script loads all three checkpoints, asserts identical key sets, verifies bit-exact equality against the base for every non-MLP tensor before any modification, computes the merge in float32 against the unmodified base (`out` is a separate dict, and `b/f1/f2` are always read from the original inputs, so no ordering hazard), casts back to the base dtype, asserts exactly 64 merged and 244 total tensors, and writes the single `model.safetensors` under the output directory. The MLP regex matches exactly the 64 named tensors per layer, and all other entries are carried over from `base` unchanged with unchanged names.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
